items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No saved script. The work is ad-hoc `python3 -c` one-liners with terse names (`dec`, `dec_wal`, `r[0]`) and no comments explaining the XOR step. The output JSON itself is clean and readable.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The project asks for a re-runnable decrypt script plus an extraction step. The agent left neither, only inline `python -c` commands in the log, so the recovery can't be re-run. The scratch copies sit in an unrelated `.gemini/.../scratch` directory.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The key `0x42` is a hardcoded constant in code, not derived from the header. Step 7 overwrites `main.db-wal` in place without checking the decrypted magic. Not checked: integrity_check, error handling.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: Derived the key from the header (`753d44c0` vs magic `377f0682`, `0x00` bytes showing as `42`). Parsed the decrypted WAL header and all 4 frames (pgno, salts). Let SQLite replay the WAL on a scratch copy first and confirmed 11 rows before writing the JSON.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: Step [1] copied `main.db` and `main.db-wal` to the scratch dir before any change. All experiments ran on copies; the `/app` WAL was only replaced in step [7]. The backup location and naming are unclear but the backup exists.
